issues.failure_explanation: The induction hypothesis gives A_t = P_t \bar A_t Q_t^\top, hence \bar A_t = P_t^\top A_t Q_t and \bar A_t \bar A_t^\top = P_t^\top (A_t A_t^\top) P_t. The proof instead uses P_t (\sum A_{t,i}A_{t,i}^\top) P_t^\top, which is generally false for non-symmetric orthogonal P_t. The subsequent algebra is built on this wrong relation.

failure_location.quote: \bar C_t^{} \bar C_t^{\top} = \sum_{i=1}^k \bar A_{t,i}^{} \bar A_{t,i}^{\top} &= P_t^{} \left( \sum_{i=1}^k A_{t,i}^{} A_{t,i}^{\top} \right) P_t^{\top}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the induction step by replacing P_t with P_t^\top (and adjusting the subsequent orthogonal factors accordingly) so that the relation between A_t and \bar A_t matches the induction hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The stated proof that the operator Sinkhorn iteration and the factor fixed-point iteration are equivalent up to orthogonal factors is invalid as written. The statement itself appears salvageable, but the paper's justification for analyzing only the factor fixed-point iteration is defective until the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Transpose error in induction proof of algorithm equivalence
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof-transcription defect. The proposition statement and the overall equivalence claim survive, and the repair does not require new proof architecture or weaken any advertised conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \chi^2 = \sup_{Y,\tilde Y \in \caC_n} \left( \frac{M(\Phi(Y),\Phi(\tilde Y))}{m(\Phi(Y),\Phi(\tilde Y))} \right) = \sup_{Y,\tilde Y \in \caC_n} \exp [ d_H(\Phi(Y), \Phi(\tilde Y))],

issues.failure_explanation: The source defines R := \chi^2 = \sup \exp d_H(\Phi(Y),\Phi(\tilde Y)), i.e. the image diameter in the Hilbert metric. The Birkhoff--Hopf contraction coefficient in terms of this R is (R-1)/(R+1), not (\sqrt R-1)/(\sqrt R+1). For R>1 the displayed \Lambda_1 is strictly smaller than the actual supremum, so the claimed Lipschitz constant is generally not valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the contraction formula by the Birkhoff--Hopf constant in terms of \chi^2 (e.g. \Lambda_1 = (\chi^2-1)/(\chi^2+1)), or redefine \chi without the square, and propagate the corrected constants to the dependent rates and ranges.
issues.overall_effect: The global convergence proof for the standard PD fixed-point iteration and the geodesic overrelaxation theorem rely on these contraction constants. The rates and, in particular, the advertised admissible range of \omega may be too optimistic as stated.
issues.title: Misstated Birkhoff--Hopf contraction constant
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, but it changes quantitative guarantees: the global convergence range and rates are weakened or altered. This is more than a pure typo because a main theorem's advertised parameter range depends on the incorrect constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bS_\omega\!\begin{pmatrix} X \\ Y \end{pmatrix} =  \begin{pmatrix} (1-\omega) X + \omega S_1(Y) \\ (1-\omega) Y + \omega S_2((1-\omega) X + \omega S_1(Y)) \end{pmatrix}

issues.failure_explanation: For overrelaxation with \omega>1, the map X \mapsto (1-\omega)X + \omega S_1(Y) is not positive definite for all X \in \caC_m, even with Y fixed in a neighborhood of Y_*. Taking X=tI with t sufficiently large makes the first component indefinite. Thus the domain cannot be the full \caC_m \times \mathcal O; only a joint neighborhood of the fixed-point orbit is guaranteed.

failure_location.quote: is well defined as a map from $\caC_m \times \mathcal O$ to $\caC_m \times \caC_n$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \caC_m \times \mathcal O by a sufficiently small neighborhood of (X_*,Y_*) (or of the whole orbit after balancing) in \caC_m \times \caC_n, or explicitly assume X is also near X_*.
issues.overall_effect: The prose overstates the local domain of the Euclidean overrelaxation map. The eventual local convergence theorem only needs a small neighborhood of the balanced fixed point, but the intermediate claim as written is false.
issues.title: Euclidean overrelaxation map claimed well-defined on too large a domain
issues.why_classification: The correction is a standard local-domain restriction. It does not affect the main local convergence theorem or the algorithms' conclusions, only the precision of a supporting prose statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the restriction $\bS_\omega' \rvert_{W_\omega}$ of $\bS_\omega'$ onto its invariant subspace $W_\omega$ has spectral radius $\rho(\omega)$ as mentioned above

issues.failure_explanation: The full linearization \bS_\omega' acts as the identity on the orbit null space V_\omega, so its full operator norm is at least 1 and is not governed by \rho(\omega)<1. The lower bound needed for the spectral radius of \bP'\bS_\omega' must use the norm of the restriction to W_\omega. The written equality with the full norm \| (\bS_\omega')^t \| is invalid, and the variable x/x_1 is also confused, so the proof of \lim \| (\bP'\bS_\omega')^t \|^{1/t} = \rho(\omega) is incomplete.

failure_location.quote: choosing $x_2 = 0$ and $x_1 \in W_\omega$ such that $\| (\bS_\omega')^t x_1 \| = \| (\bS_\omega')^t \| \| x \| \ge (\rho(\omega) - \varepsilon)^t \| x \\|$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the restriction of \bS_\omega' to W_\omega in the lower bound, choose x_1 \in W_\omega attaining (approximately) the restricted norm, and correct the notation to \|x_1\|.
issues.overall_effect: The central local convergence rate theorem is not rigorously established as written. The statement is likely true, but the displayed proof step fails to justify the lower bound.
issues.title: Flawed lower-bound step in local convergence proof
issues.why_classification: The defect is a localized proof-step error. The theorem statement, rate formula, and method survive with a short correction; no new construction or global reproof is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The Hilbert metric d_H is defined on a single positive definite cone. Here X_* \in \caC_m while Y_{t+1},Y_t \in \caC_n; if m \neq n the expression d_H(Y_{t+1},X_*) is undefined. Even when m=n, the fixed point for the Y-coordinate is Y_*, not X_*. The recursive vector inequality is therefore not a valid derivation of the claimed spectral radius bound.

failure_location.quote: d_H(Y_{t+1}, Y_*) &= d_H(Y_t \#_\omega S_2(X_{t+1}), X_*) \\ &\le \abs{1-\omega} d_H(Y_t,Y_*) + \omega \Lambda_2 d_H(X_{t+1},X_*)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace X_* by Y_* in the Y-distance estimates and in the second component of the recursive vector inequality, then repeat the spectral-radius argument.
issues.overall_effect: The global convergence proof for the geodesic overrelaxation algorithm is defective as written. The statement may be repairable, but the displayed estimate does not establish it.
issues.title: Geodesic overrelaxation proof compares Y-iterates to X_*
issues.why_classification: This is a local variable-substitution defect in the proof. The intended inequality and theorem are clear, and the repair does not change the mathematical content or require a new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With X_t=L_t^\top L_t, Y_t=R_t^\top R_t and A_{t,i}=L_t A_i R_t^\top, the residuals are L_t(\nabla_X f)L_t^\top and R_t(\nabla_Y f)R_t^\top. Their Frobenius norms equal the Frobenius gradient norm only if L_t and R_t are orthogonal. The scaling factors produced by Cholesky-based Sinkhorn iterations are not generally orthogonal, so the claimed equality is false.

failure_location.quote: It turns out that this error equals the norm of the gradient of $f$ (see~\eqref{eq: cost function}). Therefore, we call it the gradient norm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rename the quantity as a residual norm, or add an explicit orthogonal/balanced scaling convention under which the residual norm equals the gradient norm. The main convergence theorems do not depend on this equality.
issues.overall_effect: The experimental error measure is a residual norm, not the gradient norm of f. The term "gradient norm" and any interpretation of the adaptive relaxation heuristic based on gradient-norm equivalence are therefore unsupported as written.
issues.title: Residual error claimed equal to gradient norm
issues.why_classification: The defect is local to the numerical-experiment exposition. It does not invalidate the local or global convergence results, and a short renaming or added condition suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated frame-scaling conditions are inconsistent in general: taking traces gives \sum_i \|\tilde x_i\|^2 = n, while equal norms \|\tilde x_i\|=n/k give \sum_i \|\tilde x_i\|^2 = k(n/k)^2 = n^2/k, which equals n only if n=k. Moreover, the claimed correspondence \alpha_i=n\ell_i^2 does not follow from the displayed operator-scaling equations; with those equations the natural mapping is \alpha_i=\sqrt n \ell_i (up to sign) and the equal norm is \sqrt{n/k}, not n/k.

failure_location.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the frame-scaling problem with the consistent equal norm \sqrt{n/k} (or adjust the frame-operator normalization), and correct the equivalence to \alpha_i=\sqrt n \ell_i (up to signs). The experiments can then be interpreted for the corrected frame-scaling problem.
issues.overall_effect: The first numerical experiment is not correctly identified as solving the stated frame-scaling problem. The operator-scaling CP map instance is still a valid operator-scaling experiment, but the claimed equivalence to frame scaling and the interpretation of the results as frame scaling are false as written.
issues.title: Inconsistent and incorrect frame-scaling equivalence
issues.why_classification: This is more than a local typo: the stated application problem is mathematically inconsistent and the equivalence claim is wrong. However, a contained correction of the frame-scaling normalization and mapping preserves the intended application and does not affect the main operator-scaling theorems.
